# Project and Repository Plan: HW 4.4

## Part 1: HW 4.3 Project Plan

### Goal

The goal for this project is to create a quarto markdown document that satisfies the requirements of the assignment, by including the several needed sections.

#### Sub Goals

1.  Create and analyze three data tables by using and improving my old diamonds data code.
2.  Insert and analyze the Big 10 NCAA plot from my old data visualization code, applying improvements.
3.  Insert and analyze the Monte Carlo plots from my old code, making improvements and adjustments.
4.  Conduct an comparison between human-made work, AI work based on a human-made plan, and AI work based on a generic prompt.
5.  Write a reflection section.
6.  Complete an appendix detailing all uses of GenAI.
7.  Insert a properly-formatted code appendix.

### Needs

#### Nouns

- **Software:** RStudio, Quarto, R
- **Packages & Data:** tidyverse, knitr, kableExtra, diamonds, ggimage, ggrepel, patchwork, calcium.csv
- **Reference Materials:** MyOpenMath Instructions, Quarto Crash Course
- **Old Code:** Homework 3.4 Big 10 code, Homework 3.4 Monte Carlo code, Homework 3.2 Diamonds code
- **GenAI:** ChatGPT-6, ASU Image Accessibility AI Tool, generic prompt, informed prompt, ChatGPT
- **YAML Header:** author, date, title
- **Code-related:** dimensions, weight
- **Other:** narrative text, sub figure, figure, section, AI Usage appendix

#### Verbs

- **General Verbs:** open, set up, summarize, bring, write, wrangle, make, insert
- **Coding Verbs:** library(), data()

### Steps

1.  Open a Quarto Markdown document in RStudio
2.  Set up a YAML header with the proper parameters in place for a pdf format

- Make sure author, date, and title are properly set up for reproducibility purposes

3.  Set up R code chunk to load all needed packages and data for later

- Use library() and data() to bring in tidyverse, knitr, kableExtra, ggimage, ggrepel, patchwork, and diamonds

4.  Bring in the Homework 3.2 Diamonds data wrangling code, and edit it to summarize the dimensions of the diamond rather than the weight

- Add the code three times, one for each dimension, to make three tables
- Add narrative text for each table and for the overall set

5.  Bring in the Homework 3.4 Big 10 Code to recreate the NCAA plot

- Write narrative text for the plot

6.  Bring in the Homework 3.4 Monte Carlo code.

- Use it to make a figure with 4 sub figures, one for each sample size
- Use the ASU Image Accessibility Tool to get alt text for each sub figure
- Write narrative text about the Monte Carlo plot and the sub figures

7.  Conduct the comparison between generic prompt AI work, informed prompt AI work, and human work

- Write a detailed plan to wrangle the calcium.csv file and make a data visualization for it
- Download the generic prompt response and chart from the MyOpenMath instructions and insert it
- Give the plan to ChatGPT, and insert its exact response
- Use the plan to write my own code and insert it
- Use the ASU Image Accessibility Tool to generate alt text for each of the plots, inserting exact responses
- Write narrative text comparing and contrasting the three plots

8.  Write a section that conveys what I've learned throughout the course, being truly critical and reflective
9.  Create the AI Usage appendix

- Track all the alt texts I made using AI, and insert the prompts and exact responses I received for them
- Insert the exact prompts and responses used for generating the plan-informed chart from step 7

10. Add a code appendix using a proper set up to guarantee the code doesn't show up in the main part of the document

- Review appendix and fix lines that were over 80 characters

11. Review document and MyOpenMath instructions, making sure there are no major errors

- Check for proper cross referencing
- Check Quarto Crash Course to make sure techniques were applied correctly
- Fix and improve anything that needs it

12. Render the file and download it as a pdf for submission

## Part 2: HW 4.4 GitHub Repository Setup & Maintenance Plan

### Goal

The goal for this project is to create a GitHub repository for the work from Homework 4.3, and to maintain it by finding and solving issues, making commits, and having a README file.

### Needs

#### Nouns
- **Software:** GitHub, GitHub Desktop, Quarto, R Studio, Google Chrome
- **Project Files:** Homework_43.qmd, Homework_43.pdf, Homework_Plan.md, README
- **GitHub:** Homework_43_Jared repository, dev_Jared branch, commit summary, main branch, owner, Stat184-Fall2026, HW4.4 Template, issue, user, tags, pull request

#### Verbs
- **General Verbs:** open, set, add, allocate, create, write, update
- **GitHub:** commit, push, pull, reference, close

### Steps
1. Open GitHub on Google Chrome, and make a new repository, Homework_43_Jared
  - Set the owner to Stat184_Fall2026, and use the HW4.4 Template, but make sure repo is public
2. Open two issues, one to add needed files, and one to add README
  - Allocate the issues to user (me), and set proper tags
3. Create a new branch, dev_Jared for edits to go to
4. On dev_Jared, commit Homework_43.qmd, Homework_43.pdf, and Homework_Plan.md
  - Write commit summaries
5. On dev_Jared commit changes to README, updating it with project information
6. Push dev_Jared to GitHub
7. Open a pull request to merge dev_Jared into the main branch
  - Close the issues by referencing them
8. Have the main branch as the final product
  - Check for any issues before ending work
  - For an issue, make an issue, and then fix the problem, before making a commit on dev_Jared, then merge with a pull request to the main branch
